title: ZeroGR: A Generalizable and Scalable Framework for Zero-Shot Generative Retrieval
claim: A system indexes documents with generated identifiers and pseudo-queries, then retrieves by constrained decoding from a single instruction-tuned model.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, indexing then retrieval, tree diagram at right
description: Two rounded gray panels, 'Document Indexing' on the left and 'Document Retrieval' on the right, are connected by an arrow. In the left panel, a central Documents box with small icons for tables, text and code connects up to a blue Query Generator and down to a blue DocID Generator. These produce pink Pseudo Queries and teal DocID boxes, which feed an orange Instruction Tuning box. An arrow carries this to the yellow ZeroGR box in the right panel. A red Search Query box feeds ZeroGR from above. ZeroGR outputs to a Constrained Decoding panel showing a tree whose branches end in id-1, id-2 and id-3, with fading shades. A gray DocID List box sits at lower left of this panel. Pastel colors distinguish the modules.
caption: An overview of ZeroGR. Given a document collection, ZeroGR converts documents in the collection into unified DocID representations, generates diverse pseudo-queries, and builds a generative retrieval index. During online retrieval, ZeroGR decodes docids with reverse-annealed temperature scheduling to balance precision and recall.
abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) reformulates information retrieval (IR) by framing it as the generation of document identifiers (docids), thereby enabling end-to-end optimization and seamless integration with generative language models (LMs). Despite notable progress under supervised training, GR still struggles to generalize to zero-shot IR scenarios, which are prevalent in real-world applications. To tackle this challenge, we propose ZeroGR, a zero-shot generative retrieval framework that uses natural language instructions to extend GR across a wide range of IR tasks. Specifically, ZeroGR is composed of three key components: (i) an LM-based docid generator that unifies heterogeneous documents (e.g., text, tables, code) into semantically meaningful docids; (ii) an instruction-tuned query generator that generates diverse types of queries from natural language task descriptions to enhance corpus indexing; and (iii) a reverse annealing decoding strategy to balance precision and recall during docid generation. Furthermore, we introduce OpenInstIR, the most diverse open-source instructed retrieval dataset. We investigate the impact of instruction fine-tuning scale and find that performance consistently improves as the number of IR tasks encountered during training increases. Extensive experiments on the BEIR and MAIR benchmarks demonstrate that ZeroGR achieves competitive performance across a wide range of retrieval tasks, establishing a new state-of-the-art among GR methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/sunnweiwei/ZeroGR.
